desc:
WooCommerce plugin maintenance and updates keep your plugin working as WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP change. Ecom Swift LLC runs a one-time care sprint: compatibility tests, bug fixes, updated headers and libraries, and a short health report.

## What is WooCommerce plugin maintenance?

It is the routine work that keeps an existing plugin compatible with its surroundings. That means testing against new WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP releases, fixing warnings and bugs, refreshing libraries and updating the tested-up-to values that tell users the plugin is current.

This service is a single starter sprint, not a monthly plan. It brings a neglected plugin up to date and shows you what regular care would need to cover.

## Why do plugins break when nothing in them changed?

A plugin is only one part of a moving system. WooCommerce introduces new ways to store orders and new checkout components. WordPress adds new APIs and removes old ones. PHP versions deprecate features that older code depends on. The plugin file stays the same, but its environment changes under it.

Warnings often appear first, then errors. A store owner sees a notice in the admin, a log fills with deprecation messages or a screen turns blank after a hosting upgrade. By then, support tickets are already arriving.

## How regular upkeep protects installs and trust

Store owners judge a plugin by how current it looks. A tested-up-to value from many releases ago makes people hesitate to install. Reviews of old plugins often mention that things stopped working.

Upkeep also protects the people who already use you. Fixing a bug found in support tickets prevents the next ten identical tickets. Updating a library with a known flaw reduces risk for every store running your code.

## What a good care sprint includes

- A test of the plugin on the latest WooCommerce, WordPress and PHP versions.
- Fixes for warnings, notices and deprecated function calls.
- Bug fixes taken from your real support requests.
- Updated tested-up-to headers once testing passes.
- Updated libraries and dependencies.
- Update testing on a staging copy with existing data.
- A quick security scan for common problems.
- A check of order storage and block checkout compatibility, in higher packages.
- A release package with a changelog.
- A short health report with what was fixed and what remains.

## What we do

We set up a staging site with the newest WooCommerce and WordPress and run your plugin through its main flows. We turn on debug logging and note every warning. We read your recent support requests, if you share them, to find patterns such as the same bug reported many times.

After that, we fix issues in order of importance and test again. You receive the updated code or zip, a changelog and the health report. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of issues fixed, whether support-ticket bugs and library updates are included, and whether a PHP version upgrade and a release package are added. Ongoing monthly care is quoted separately.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share recent support requests so we can find repeated problems.
- Tell us the oldest PHP version you still support.
- Keep a copy of the current release before we start.
- Update the changelog every time you publish.
- Plan a repeat check after each major WooCommerce release.

**Avoid:**
- Bumping the tested-up-to value without testing.
- Ignoring deprecation warnings because the store still works.
- Updating libraries on the live site first.
- Running several unrelated changes in one release.
- Waiting for a crash before looking at the plugin.

## Who this service is for

This service suits an author whose plugin has not been updated for a while and now shows warnings. It suits a company that bought a plugin and needs it brought current before taking over support. It also suits an owner of a plugin on the public directory who has received reports of problems after recent updates.

## What we need from you

Send the plugin code or repository access, the list of support requests and a note on which versions you support. We never ask for passwords. Access is given as a collaborator or developer user, and a live store is not needed. If your plugin is in the public directory, we prepare the update and you publish it from your own account.
